text.p: These are significant stories in the Nigerian press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Petroleum Trust Fund, which disburses money from pump price increases in 1994, is coming to the rescue of National Electricity Power Authority by financing a project to supply electricity to rural areas.
- The Nigerian Stock Exchange is worried about a new stock exchange to be located in the new capital Abuja.
- Finance ministry may have set up a committee to probe the Security and Exchange Commission, which regulates the capital market.
- Five thousand policemen put on alert to forestall any disturbances during the fourth anniversary of the annulled June 12, 1993 presidential elections.

- The petrol scarcity in Nigeria may linger for sometime as vital raw materials imported for operation of Warri oil refinery have not yet been cleared because of disagreement between the refinery company and the customs department.
- More than 800 cartons of expired biscuits imported from India were burnt at the weekend by the Standard Organisation of Nigeria.
- In a renewed war on money laundering, the central bank has set up a surveilance committee to monitor some banks suspected to have been aiding fraudsters.

- Nigeria may initiate moves to counteract a diplomatic initiatives by soldiers who seized power in Sierra Leone to win foreign sympathy for their ouster of the elected government which Nigeria wants reinstated.
- Nigerian conglomerate UAC has acquired Grand Cereals and Oil Mills Limited for 640 million naira.
- Banks raise deposit rates to source funds to refund cancelled forex purchases.
- Nigerian footballer Joseph Dosu survives car crash.
